report.source_text: Upon admission, laboratory tests showed: urinary protein 4+, red blood cells 71.9/uL, white blood cells 1.8/uL; 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g; serum albumin 16.5 g/l; serum creatinine 63 µmol/L (corresponding to an estimated glomerular filtration rate of 123 mL/min/1.73 m² as calculated by the CKD-EPI equation); hemoglobin 115 g/L; white blood cell counts 3.68 × 10^9/L; mature lymphocyte counts 0.81 × 10^9/L; platelets were normal. CD4 + T cell counts: 77/Ul (reference range, 441–2156/uL); CD8 + T cell counts: 339/uL (reference range,125–1312/uL); CD4/CD8+: 0.23 (reference range, 0.71–2.78); NK cell counts 49/uL (reference range, 95–640/uL). TSH: 24.90 mIU/L, FT3: 3.44pmol/L, TT4: 53.80nmol/L, thyroglobulin: 52.40ng/Ml. Anti-nuclear antibody 1:100, anti-double-stranded DNA antibody with titer of 25.4/IU. All extractable nuclear antigen (ENA) test were negative. The complement C3 levels were reduced to 0.58 g/L, while complement C4 0.17 g/L was within the normal range. Subsequent investigations disclosed that the serum immunoglobulin G (IgG) concentration was markedly diminished, registering at 4.51 g/L. The assays for anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA), anti-glomerular basement membrane (GBM) antibody, serum anti-M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R) antibody, Coombs’test, antiphospholipid antibody, immunofixation electrophoresis, and tumor biomarkers all manifested negative findings. The viral serological screenings for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and rubella virus (RV) exhibited equivocal results. The diagnostic tests for hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV), syphilis, and HIV were all negative. Bone marrow flow cytometry analysis did not identify any conspicuous aberrant hematopoietic lymphocytes and plasma cells. Whole-genome sequencing failed to detect any genetic polymorphisms or mutations.

The renal biopsy pathology is the definitive diagnostic evidence needed to confirm the diagnosis.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old Chinese male chef presented with a 6-month history of persistent foamuria and progressive generalized edema, accompanied by scattered verrucous hyperplasia on limbs and face (more prominent on feet). Physical examination revealed severe pitting edema with mild verrucous hyperplasia on face and upper extremities, and severe coalescing lesions on lower extremities. Laboratory investigations at admission demonstrated nephrotic-range proteinuria (4.5 g/24h, 4+ on urinalysis), hematuria (71.9 RBC/µL), pyuria (1.8 WBC/µL), hypoalbuminemia (16.5 g/L), and preserved renal function (serum creatinine 63 µmol/L, eGFR 123 mL/min/1.73m²). Serologic evaluation revealed positive ANA (1:100), positive anti-dsDNA antibody (25.4 IU), reduced complement C3 (0.58 g/L), and markedly diminished serum IgG (4.51 g/L). Severe immunologic abnormalities were documented: CD4+ T cell lymphopenia (77/µL), inverted CD4/CD8 ratio (0.23), and NK cell lymphopenia (49/µL). Additional findings included thyroid dysfunction (TSH 24.90 mIU/L, elevated thyroglobulin) and negative testing for ANCA, anti-GBM, anti-PLA2R, and viral serologies (HSV, RV, HBV, HCV, EBV, CMV, syphilis, HIV). Renal biopsy pathology confirmed class V lupus nephritis. During one-year follow-up, the patient developed deep vein thrombosis, acute kidney injury, and cytomegalovirus infection, with persistent proteinuria and expanding verrucous lesions. CD4+ T cell count remained persistently below 150 cells/µL despite prednisone tapering to 7.5 mg/day and near-quiescent lupus activity, leading to consideration of concurrent Idiopathic CD4+ Lymphopenia (ICL).

Serologic evidence of systemic lupus erythematosus: ANA 1:100, anti-dsDNA 25.4 IU, reduced C3 (0.58 g/L), markedly diminished IgG (4.51 g/L)

Negative testing for ANCA, anti-GBM, anti-PLA2R, ENA panel, and viral serologies (HSV, RV, HBV, HCV, EBV, CMV, syphilis, HIV)
Pathological diagnosis of class V lupus nephritis confirmed by renal biopsy
Clinical progression during one-year follow-up with deep vein thrombosis, acute kidney injury, cytomegalovirus infection, persistent proteinuria, and expanding verrucous lesions

Negative viral serologies for HSV, RV, HBV, HCV, EBV, CMV, syphilis, and HIV (E003)
